items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: He's -- he asked me to come down some Sundays, you know

ctx.x: like to call him "True Student" to myself, you see, because he's a reverend. And my life was saved by a reverend when I was a child, see, because I didn't know nothing about the Swanee River, see. That's how I was baptized. But it was a different body of water. And, like the dark (unintelligible) you see, I wasn't -- I didn't know how to see the light in the dark at that time. But I eventually did.

So, anyway not to speak too much about me as a tap dancer, but I am a kind of an example of what I'm speaking of here about the Reverend -- Jazz Vespers, you see. See, he's John too, you know. He's -- he asked me to come down some Sundays, you know, and this is -- to kind of make his message more open, you know, and to outlet the freedom that the land of the free is all about, you see.

And so, I tries to tap dance for him. I tried to story tap, you see -- I call it because it's like we are supposed to read some kind of passions in the day's lessons each day, you see, especially on the day of rest, see.
